//: TODO(design): first batch of events, written by Claude for M5 (GAME_DESIGN.md §10, §14); texts and numbers are working values, change them freely. An event happens when the hydra steps on an event site on the map (balance.json undergroundGenerator.rings[].eventSites). Of the events that fit (conditions, as in dialogues.json), those with the highest priority are drawn by weight. once: happens at most once in a hydra's life (default true). A step of a mini quest also has notFlags with its own flags, so that a step done in an earlier generation doesn't come again (the quest's flags are world knowledge, flags.json). quest: the mini quest the event is a step of (steps are chained by flags: a step sets a flag, the next step needs it). A choice can need a head (needsHead: class id) or a condition on the hydra (needsCondition: world.json conditions, e.g. warmed), cost resources (cost), and either have one outcome, or be a gamble: chance (0–1) of success, otherwise failure. An outcome has a text and may: give or take muck, moisture, bones; change the alert; heal or hurt the body (bodyHp) and every head (headsHp, never below 1); put a condition on the hydra (condition, world.json); show the map around (reveal: hexes); start a battle (battle: an encounter group, enemies.json); set flags (setFlags); start a dialogue (dialogue: an id from dialogues.json); grow a head (newHead: class id); have the Cinderkin melt a tunnel through the rock nearby (bore: true; how, in world.json thresholds.cinderBore); give the hydra a mutation for her and her heiresses (mutation: an id from mutations.json). FTL-style (2026-11-16, TODO(design)). A number of muck, moisture, bones, alert, bodyHp or headsHp can be a range [min, max], rolled when it happens: "muck": [4, 9]. An outcome can go on: "then": { "choices": [...] } is a next scene of the same event, with the outcome's text above its choices (the event ends at an outcome without then). drawChoices: n on an event (or in a then) shows only n of its choices, drawn at random each time; a choice with "always": true is always among them (keep a free choice always shown). A lead: "lead": { "event": "<event id>", "distance": [12, 20] } puts a new event site with that event this many hexes away, marked on the map. byLeadOnly: true on an event means it only happens where a lead put it.

events.title: A Novice with a Checklist
events.text: A novice of the Order of the Eternal Flame is inspecting this cave for heresy. He has a checklist. He has reached 'hydra' and is looking for a pencil.

outcome.text: He tasted of chalk and diligence. Someone will notice the inspections have stopped.
He wanders off, writing 'no hydra observed' with great confidence.

success.text: He ticks 'cave: damp' and leaves, satisfied with a job well done.

failure.text: He ticks 'hydra: yes' and blows a whistle. Two more novices arrive, both with torches.

events.title: A Certified Relic
events.text: A wooden box on a ledge, sealed with the Order's wax. The certificate inside swears it holds the left toe of Saint Cinder. It is the fourth left toe of Saint Cinder you have heard of.

outcome.text: It is, against all odds, a toe. Holy or not, it goes down well.
A pig's toe. The certificate, however, is perfectly genuine. The box is good for scrap.
Somewhere above, a pilgrimage is planned around this ledge. You have time.

events.title: Groaning Rock
events.text: The ceiling here creaks like an old man getting up. Small stones patter down. Something larger is thinking about it.

success.text: Nothing falls. The rock sighs behind you, disappointed.

failure.text: A boulder lands on the body. The heads argue about whose idea it was to hurry.

outcome.text: The ceiling settles. From the steady ledge you can see a good way down the tunnels.

events.title: The Drummer
events.text: A man sits in the dark, beating a drum made from his own shield. Every beat is slightly wrong. 'You hear it too,' he says. 'The song. It's out of tune. I am fixing it.' He is not fixing it.

success.text: For a moment the beats line up, and the heads hear something vast breathe in. The tunnels around you feel very clear.

failure.text: The wrong beat crawls into every skull at once. The heads spend the rest of the day arguing about rhythm.

outcome.text: The drum keeps going for a while on its own.
Behind you the beat goes on, wrong, and certain of itself.

events.title: Nine Candles
events.text: Nine unlit candles in a circle around a bowl of fish heads. A note in a shaky hand: 'For the Many-Headed. One candle for each head, when you have nine. We are patient.'

outcome.text: The heads count the candles, then each other. They arrive at different numbers.
Someone will come back and find it untouched. Somehow, that will mean a great deal to them.

events.title: A Warning in Chalk
events.text: Chalk on the wall: a serpent with one head, and next to it a hydra, crossed out nine times. Underneath, in capitals: THE SERPENT IS ONE. The chalk dust on the floor is fresh.

choices.text: Add a few heads to the serpent.

outcome.text: Better. The heads argue over whose likeness it is.
The chalk hisses off the wall, and a good deal of the wall goes with it. Underneath is softer, older rock.
You leave the wall as it is. It watches you go, with one eye.

events.title: A Warm Crack
events.text: The rock here is warm to the touch, and humming. Something inside is eating the heat, a little at a time, with many small mouths.

outcome.text: Warm, for the first time in a long time. The humming moves closer. You leave before it gets ideas, and take the warmth with you.
The humming stops. Then it starts again, further off, offended. The cooled rock cracks open onto a lookout.
Some doors are best left humming.

events.title: The Cinderkin
events.text: A swarm seeps out of a crack: insects of hot rock, each the size of a grain of rice and twice as hot. They circle you once, tasting the air, and settle on the wall to wait. They eat heat. They do not seem to mind where it comes from.

outcome.text: They find the warmth in your hide, and follow it into the rock like water into sand. Somewhere nearby, the rock begins to glow.
None of the heads can light a fire. You are a swamp. The Cinderkin light it themselves, eat it, and go looking for seconds. Somewhere nearby, the rock begins to glow.
Hot. Very hot. The Biter announces that it meant to do that. The swarm leaves, offended.
A thousand tiny glowing eyes watch you go, then go back to watching the rock.

events.title: The Tithe Box
events.text: An iron box bolted to the rock. On its lid: TITHES FOR THE ETERNAL FLAME. TEN PARTS IN A HUNDRED. RECEIPTS ISSUED.

outcome.text: Inside: a small fortune in muck and a receipt book. The Order will want the book back.
A receipt slides out of a slot. It thanks you for your contribution to the burning of your swamp.

events.title: A Ring of Pale Caps
events.text: A perfect circle of pale mushrooms. Inside it the dust lies very still, and time seems to be holding its breath. Something on the far side of the air is looking back.

success.text: For one long moment the heads are a single body and agree on everything. Afterwards they argue about who agreed first. The mycelium keeps whispering.

failure.text: Too many songs at once. Something with too many eyes says something kind, and it is the worst thing the heads have ever heard.

outcome.text: It tastes of earth and of the colour green. Afterwards the heads hear things a long way off. Some of them are even there.
Wise. The ring looks almost disappointed.

events.title: A Lost Pilgrim
events.text: A pilgrim of the Order, lost for days. He has eaten his candles. He asks, very politely, which way is up.

outcome.text: He thanks you and leaves to tell everyone about the kind monster. Nobody will believe the kind part.
He thanks you and walks deeper. The Order will search for him in all the wrong places.
He was mostly candle.

events.title: A Pillar of Salt
events.text: A man made of salt, caught mid-step, holding a lantern made of salt. A plaque at his feet: BROTHER OSRIC, WHO WAS TOLD TO WAIT HERE. He is still waiting.

outcome.text: Salt. Very loyal salt. Your hide stiffens.
The hand comes off with the lantern. Brother Osric does not complain. He is still waiting.
Somebody should come back for him. Nobody will.

events.title: An Old Skull
events.text: A skull with too many eye sockets, half sunk in the mud. Not human. Not quite yours. The teeth match your own.

outcome.text: None of the heads knows the words, so they hum something instead. For a moment it sounds like someone else's song.
Old marrow, dry as paper. Nobody says anything for a while. That night the necks ache, and in the morning they are thicker.

events.title: An Old Wallow
events.text: A hollow of mud so old it has gone black and soft as velvet. Something large wallowed here for a very long time, and left its smell behind as a kind of will.

outcome.text: The smell soaks in past the scales and stays. The heads complain about it, then stop noticing, which is worse.
Good mud. Old mud. It keeps its shape in the jaw.
Someone else's smell is someone else's business.

events.title: A Vein of Strange Salt
events.text: A vein of salt that glitters blue-green, licked smooth by something with a very long tongue. A sign of the Order: DO NOT LICK. Beneath it, in another hand: WE KNOW.

success.text: The salt tingles down the spine, and the spine stretches to follow it. There is more of you now, at both ends.

failure.text: The salt bites back. Every tongue goes numb, and the heads take turns blaming each other's.

outcome.text: DO NOT LICK. WE KNOW. The heads feel known.
Somebody has to obey the signs. Today it is you.

events.title: An Empty Egg
events.text: Half an eggshell, big as a cauldron, with the smell of your own kind still on it. Something hatched here long ago and left without cleaning up.

outcome.text: It goes down in pieces. Later the heads swear they can hear another one, very small, waiting its turn.
It still fits, more or less. Everyone sleeps better for it.
Whoever it was, they are not coming back for it.

events.title: A Carving in the Rock
events.text: Carved into the wall: tall figures, or long ones, it is hard to say, standing around a coiled shape. Their mouths are open. Beneath them run rows of marks like notes of music. Or teeth.

outcome.text: Each head reads the marks differently. One hears a lullaby, one a warning, one a shopping list. They agree it is important.

choices.text: Copy the marks onto a scale.

outcome.text: A precise copy, etched into a scale. A little itchy. The marks seem to point somewhere further in.
Old scratches on an old wall. The underground is full of them.

events.title: The Cold Machine
events.text: A machine of brass pipes and stone bellows, taller than the hydra, grown over with moss. Pipes run down into the rock, toward something warm. The coiled shape from the carving is hammered into its side. It is silent, but only just.

outcome.text: The pipes cough mist, then hold one low note. Far below, something turns over in its sleep.

success.text: It shudders and hums a single note. Then it sulks. Far below, something stirs.

failure.text: A pipe bursts. Scalding steam, and an echo that carries a long way.

outcome.text: Good metal. The machine lets out a long, thin whistle as it comes apart, like someone remembering a tune too late.

events.title: The Last Note
events.text: A round chamber with walls too smooth for any tool. In the middle lies a mask with no mouth, made for a face longer than any human's. As you come near, the whole room hums the note the machine played.

outcome.text: The note opens like a door. For one heartbeat you understand the song. Then the heartbeat ends, but the tunnels around stay clear in your mind.

choices.text: Take the mask to Old Mother Toad.

outcome.text: It weighs nothing. The heads take turns carrying it, and none of them wants a turn.
It tastes of nothing at all. The humming stops. Everyone pretends not to be relieved.

events.title: A Surveyor's Stake
events.text: A red-painted stake, a measuring chain, and a sign: THIS CAVE IS THE PROPERTY OF THE ORDER OF THE ETERNAL FLAME, PENDING SURVEY. TRESPASSERS WILL BE CATALOGUED.

outcome.text: The chain runs off into the dark, marked every ten yards in neat red paint.

choices.text: Move the stake a few yards.

outcome.text: According to the Order, this cave is now slightly smaller.
It tastes of red paint and good intentions.

events.title: The Surveyors
events.text: Three surveyors of the Order sit round a lantern, arguing over a map. The map is upside down. One of them sees you and writes something down.

outcome.text: The surveyors drop the map and pick up torches. Two of them, anyway. The third keeps writing.

success.text: They measure every neck, twice. The report will call you 'a large damp nuisance, not a priority'.

failure.text: They measure every neck, twice, and then they count the necks. They count again. One of them runs.

outcome.text: The Acid Spitter cannot bear an upside-down map. It turns it the right way up, then makes a few improvements. The surveyors leave to chart a lake that is not there.

events.title: The Survey Office
events.text: A camp table in the dark: ink, wax, the seal of the Order and a stack of forms. A sign on the table: SUBTERRANEAN SURVEY OFFICE. CLOSED FOR PRAYER.

outcome.text: Officially, this hydra has been seen to. It says so in red wax.
Neat, careful maps, every one of them wrong in a different and useful way.
The Order will have to fill them all in again. It is the cruellest thing you have ever done.

events.//: M4: events on the surface name its biome (conditions.biomes); the others happen only underground.
events.title: A Scarecrow in a Tabard
events.text: In the middle of a field stands a scarecrow in the tabard of the Order. Someone has painted on a stern face. The crows have not been told.

outcome.text: Straw and a tabard. The heads agree it was the most honest member of the Order they have met.

choices.text: Put its hat on The Spare.

outcome.text: The Spare wears it all day. A patrol passes at a distance and salutes.
It keeps watch over the field. It has never caught anything, and it is not about to start.

events.title: The Village Well
events.text: A well at the edge of a village, a bucket on a rope, and a sign: BLESSED BY THE ORDER. DO NOT SPIT.

outcome.text: The heads drink in turns, then all at once. The village will want to know where its water went.
The Acid Spitter reads the sign twice, then spits. The Order will have to come and bless it all over again, and it has better things to do.
You leave it. The sign seems disappointed.

events.title: Pilgrims on the Road
events.text: Three pilgrims walk to a Flame Shrine with lanterns and a hymn. They have not seen you. The hymn has a verse about you, and it is not flattering.

outcome.text: The hymn stops in the middle of the verse. The shrine will wait for its pilgrims a long time.
They walk into the mist and come out at the river, lanterns out. They agree it was a sign.

success.text: The heads hum the tune. The pilgrims hurry on, and swear afterwards that the hills were singing.

failure.text: One head sings the words. The pilgrims drop their lanterns and run for the castle.

events.title: A Field
events.text: A ploughed field under the open sky. Nothing happens here, which up here is called farming.

outcome.text: Warm earth. The heads lie very still and pretend to be a hedge.
Turnips, mostly. And worms, which are better.

events.//: FTL-style events per land (2026-11-16, TODO(design)): each underground biome has its own; some lead on to a second scene, some roll their rewards, some draw their choices, some leave a lead on the map.
events.title: The Drowned Bell
events.text: A bell of the Order hangs from a beam under the water. The current swings it, slowly, and it rings once every few breaths. Somebody above must still be wondering where the sound comes from.

success.text: One great note rolls out through the flooded halls and comes back from very far away, with the shape of the tunnels in it.

failure.text: One great note rolls out through the flooded halls and up a shaft, into the ears of a sexton who writes it down.

outcome.text: The beam gives before the Biter does. Bronze, and a nest of things that lived inside the bell and now live inside you.
It rings on behind you, once every few breaths, for nobody.

events.title: Eels in Session
events.text: Forty eels lie in a circle in the shallows. One of them is speaking, at length. As you come closer they all turn, and the speaking one says, 'The chair recognises the member with several heads.'

outcome.text: The motion before the session: that the hydra is, for the purposes of the water rights, an eel. The heads look at each other.

choices.text: Argue that you are mostly eel.

success.text: Carried, thirty-one to nine. You are granted the water rights of an eel, which turn out to be generous.

failure.text: The motion fails on a point of order raised by a very old eel. The heads argue about it for the rest of the day.

outcome.text: The session is adjourned. The eels elect a new chair at once, and he is much more agreeable.
Your abstention is noted, at length. You leave before the minutes are read.
Behind you the eel resumes speaking, from the beginning.

events.title: A Floating Ledger
events.text: A ledger of the Order drifts past on the current, swollen to twice its size. FLOOD DAMAGE, LOWER STORES, it says on the cover. Someone has underlined LOWER three times.

outcome.text: The Acid Spitter reads it aloud, correcting the spelling. The lower stores are not lost, only under water. The page has a little map.

choices.text: Fish it out and look at the pictures.

success.text: Mostly sums, but on one page there is a little map, with a cross and a drawing of a sad monk.

failure.text: It falls apart in your jaws. The heads agree it was probably boring.

outcome.text: Somewhere downstream, a clerk is going to have a very bad day.

events.title: The Sunken Stores
events.text: The lower stores of the Order, exactly where the ledger said: barrels of lamp oil, sacks of something, and a monk's sandal floating in the doorway on its own. Everything is wet, and everything is still here.

outcome.text: Lamp oil for the muck, salt pork for the body. The Order will write to itself about this.

choices.text: Take only what won't be missed.

outcome.text: You take the sandal and one sack nobody had written down. Very tidy.

events.title: A Reflection
events.text: Still water, black as a mirror. The hydra in it has a different number of heads. Each of your heads counts them, and gets a different answer.

success.text: The hydra in the water nods, once, as if to someone behind you. Your necks feel stronger for having been counted.

failure.text: The hydra in the water looks back at you, and then, slowly, away. Nobody sleeps well after that.

outcome.text: The surface clouds over. The Mist Breather says it was only being polite, and that the other one started it.
The heads do not look, all together, which is a first.

events.title: The Root Confessional
events.text: A novice of the Order has wedged himself into a knot of roots and is confessing to them. He has been at it some time. The roots seem to be listening; one of them has grown into his ear.

outcome.text: He confesses to lying about vespers, to coveting a candle, and to having seen a hydra and told no one. Then he notices you.
You nod gravely, all of you. He weeps with relief, and swears never to mention you to anyone, which he keeps.

success.text: The heads confess each other's sins, in detail. The novice flees. The roots seem pleased, and loosen around a cache of old bones.

failure.text: The heads confess each other's sins, in detail, and then it becomes a fight. The roots take sides.

outcome.text: Penance, of a kind.
The Strangler unwinds the roots with professional respect. The novice runs, leaving his satchel and a strong opinion of you.
He is on to his childhood now. It will be a while.

events.title: Hanging Pods
events.text: Fat seed pods hang from the roots overhead, each the size of a head, each a different colour. Some of them are humming.

success.text: Sweet and hot. The body warms right through.

failure.text: Very hot. Much too hot. The heads breathe out steam for an hour.

outcome.text: Cold and wet inside, like a cave in a skin.

success.text: It tastes of nothing, and then of everything you have ever eaten. The heads remember things they had better have forgotten, among them the way here.

failure.text: It tastes of nothing, and then of Old Mother Toad's cooking. Nobody speaks of it.

success.text: The humming goes down and keeps on humming, lower, in the belly. It is not unpleasant. It may be permanent.

failure.text: The humming goes down, and comes back up, louder, in a different key.

outcome.text: The pods sway after you, humming among themselves.

events.title: Knotted Prayers
events.text: Ribbons of the Order are tied to the roots here, one every few yards, each with a prayer stitched on it. FOR THOSE WHO WALK THE ROOTS. FOR THOSE THE ROOTS WALK. FOR BROTHER EADMER, WHO WENT AHEAD.

outcome.text: They lead deeper, one after another, until you know where they are going even without them.
Linen and good intentions. Not filling.
Behind you the ribbons stir, though there is no wind.

events.title: Brother Eadmer, Who Went Ahead
events.text: At the end of the ribbons sits Brother Eadmer, or most of him. The roots have taken the rest. He is perfectly calm. 'Ah,' he says. 'Are you the next brother? You have more heads than they said.'

choices.text: Say you are the next brother.

outcome.text: He gives you his blessing, his rosary and the key to a chest the roots have long since eaten. The rosary is mostly bone.
The roots let him go reluctantly, and he walks off in the wrong direction, singing. The Order will count him as a miracle.
'Tell them I went ahead,' he says. The roots tighten, kindly.

events.title: The Gardener of the Ninefold
events.text: A thin woman is training roots into a shape with nine long necks. She has been at it for years. When she sees you she drops her shears and kneels, and then gets up again, because her knees are not what they were.

outcome.text: You admire it from all angles at once. She cries a little, and gives you everything in her basket.
'Only that you live,' she says, 'and grow, and that one day there are nine of you, and then the song will have a chorus.' She draws you a map to a quiet place.

events.title: The Ossuary Audit
events.text: A friar of the Order sits among the stacked skulls with an abacus and a ledger. 'Four thousand and eleven,' he says, without looking up. 'It should be four thousand and fourteen. Someone has been at the bones.'

outcome.text: He hands you the abacus. You count with him for an hour. It comes to four thousand and eleven, then four thousand and twelve, then he looks at your heads and goes very quiet.
He enters you in the ledger, carefully, as three assets. The books balance. He thanks you and leaves, and the Order will find nothing wrong.

choices.text: Take the three missing ones yourselves.

outcome.text: The books will never balance now, which keeps him busy for the rest of his life.
The Glutton eats the abacus, bead by bead. The friar watches the last of his arithmetic go down and resigns on the spot.

choices.text: Take a few bones on the way past.

outcome.text: Four thousand and eight, says the friar, behind you, in a very small voice.
You go quietly. Four thousand and eleven, he says again.

events.title: Epitaphs, Reasonable Rates
events.text: A gravedigger sits by a pile of headstones with no names on them yet. He chisels in his sleep. 'Epitaphs,' he says. 'Written in advance. The song tells me who will need which.' He has a few that would fit you.

outcome.text: He hands it over. It is very light for a stone. The Order forgets a little of what it knew about you.
Under the stone, by long tradition, is a little food for the dead. You are the dead, for the time being.
On the back of the stone is a map, scratched in by someone who did.
The heads read it to each other several times. They feel better about everything.
He winks, and lifts the corner of the stone. Muck, a great deal of it, owed to somebody.
'They all say that,' he says, and goes back to chiselling. You glimpse your name on the next stone.

events.title: A Sealed Sarcophagus
events.text: A stone coffin with the lid chained down. On the lid, a notice of the Order: DO NOT OPEN. THE OCCUPANT HAS BEEN DEALT WITH. Underneath, scratched from the inside: NOT ENTIRELY.

success.text: Inside is a long-dead abbot and everything he was buried with, which was a great deal. He has no objection.

failure.text: Inside is a long-dead abbot who has some objections. By the time he has made them all, every head is bleeding and the Order heard the shouting.

choices.text: Read the rest of the scratching.

outcome.text: The Acid Spitter dissolves the grime. Under NOT ENTIRELY, smaller: LEFT HIS RING IN THE NORTH CHAPEL. TELL NO ONE. And then a little map of the crypts.
From inside the coffin, very faintly, a sigh of disappointment.

events.title: The Abbot's Ring
events.text: A small chapel, sealed for a hundred years, and on its altar a ring with a stone the size of an egg. The Order's records call it lost. The Order's records are about to be right.

outcome.text: It goes down cold and stays cold, a little stone moon in the belly. Things in the dark seem to notice you less.

choices.text: Pry out the stone and trade the rest.

outcome.text: Gold is only mud that shines, the heads agree, and mud is useful.

events.title: A Choir of One
events.text: In a burial niche, a skeleton in a choir robe stands with its jaw open. Air moves through the crypt and through it, and it sings: one long note, slightly flat. The heads all want to correct it.

outcome.text: The Screamer gives it the right note. The skeleton falls to pieces with relief, and somewhere a long way below, something else falls silent too.

success.text: Two flat notes make a strange chord, and the crypt opens up to the ear: every passage and turning sounds out at once.

failure.text: Two flat notes make a terrible chord. A brother of the Order upstairs drops a tray.

outcome.text: It sings on behind you, flat, and faithful.

events.title: The Salt Excise
events.text: A clerk of the Order sits at a folding desk in the middle of the mine. A sign: SALT EXCISE. ALL SALT LEAVING THIS MINE IS SUBJECT TO DUTY. He looks at you. He looks at the salt on your scales. He takes out a form.

outcome.text: He stamps your scales. You are now a legal export of the Order. Patrols will wave you through, for a while.
The Screamer contests it at length, and at volume. The clerk files a complaint against himself and leaves the desk to you.
Undeclared. The Order notices its clerks, if not its salt.
He writes something down. You suspect it is your description.

events.title: A Brine Spring
events.text: Water wells up through a crack in the salt floor, clear as glass. Bubbles rise in it, though nothing is breathing down there that you know of.

success.text: Salty but sweet underneath. Your belly fills like a cistern.

failure.text: All salt, and then more salt. Your hide crackles as it dries.

outcome.text: The salt draws the ache out of old wounds. It also draws out a fair amount of skin.
The bubbles keep rising. Something down there is patient.

events.title: The Last Shift
events.text: A miner is digging at the end of an old gallery with his bare hands. His pick is long gone, and most of his nails. 'It's just behind here,' he says. 'The song. I can hear it in the salt. One more shift.'

choices.text: Listen at the rock with him.

outcome.text: The heads press to the salt. There is something: a rhythm, very faint, very deep, and very wrong, like a heartbeat with a stammer.

success.text: The salt gives way into a gallery nobody has seen for centuries. The miner walks into it, singing, and does not come back. You can see a long way from here.

failure.text: The salt gives way, and so does the ceiling. The miner is not seen again. Neither, for a while, is your tail.

outcome.text: He fights, then weeps, then sleeps. When he wakes he tells you where the miners hid their stores before the Order took the mine.
Behind you the scraping goes on. It keeps time, almost.
Behind you the scraping goes on. It keeps time, almost.

events.title: The Miners' Cache
events.text: Behind a false wall of salt bricks: the miners' cache, hidden from the Order the year it took the mine. Tools, lamp oil, dried fish, and a little wooden hydra somebody carved, with nine heads, for luck.

outcome.text: The fish is a hundred years old and still good, which says something about salt.
The heads pass it round and argue over which of them it looks like. Somewhere, the Ninefold would approve.

events.title: The Communion
events.text: A hollow full of soft blue light, where the spores hang in the air so thick they have weather. Spirals turn in it, slowly, and the spirals have a sound, and the sound has a colour.

outcome.text: The heads breathe in together. For a moment there is one hydra, very large, and very calm. Then the spiral opens like an eye.

success.text: At the centre of the spiral is the song, coiled, and every root and thread of the Deeps hums along with it. You know where everything moves, for a while.

failure.text: At the centre of the spiral is another spiral, and another, and the heads come back one at a time, and not in the right order.

choices.text: Look back the way you came.

outcome.text: From inside the light, the whole of the Deeps is laid out like a drawing. Something on the far side of the drawing is looking too, and waves.
The heads come out coughing blue. They agree it was wonderful, and refuse to say why.
You go round it with every mouth shut. The light dims a little, offended.

events.title: A Cap That Trades
events.text: A mushroom as tall as a man, with a cap like a shopkeeper's awning. When you come close it speaks, in a voice made of rustling. 'Memories,' it says. 'I trade in memories. Yours for mine. Fair rates.'

choices.text: Trade the memory of the lair.

outcome.text: You remember the lair perfectly well afterwards, but not how it smelled. In return the cap gives you the tunnels around it.

choices.text: Trade the memory of your mother.

outcome.text: Something goes quiet in the heads, and something grows in the body instead. They don't talk about it.

choices.text: Trade the memory of the Order.

success.text: Without it you move through the dark a little easier, and the Order seems to have forgotten you back.

failure.text: You forget them, but they do not forget you. You walk straight past a warning sign you no longer understand.

outcome.text: It takes the hunger, and gives you a heap of the stuff it grows in.
'Oh,' says the cap, 'this one is good.' It gives you a whole lake's worth of dew.
'Everyone does, at first,' says the cap.

events.title: The Knight Who Walks Slowly
events.text: A knight of the Order walks past you, very slowly, in full armour. Pale threads grow out of his visor and his gauntlets. He is going somewhere with great purpose, one step a minute. He does not look round.

outcome.text: It takes a long time. Eventually you see where he is going, and it is somewhere the mycelium wants seen.

success.text: Crunchy outside, soft inside. The threads were only on the surface. Mostly.

failure.text: The threads were not only on the surface. For an hour one of the heads walks very slowly, with great purpose.

outcome.text: He walks on. Somewhere ahead, something has been waiting for him for a long time.

events.title: The Garden Below
events.text: Where the knight was going: a garden of white threads, laid out in rings around a dozen other knights of the Order, all standing perfectly still, all slowly flowering. It is beautiful. It is very quiet. It is also, the heads note, a larder.

outcome.text: The flowers taste of iron and of a very long sleep. Afterwards the Deeps seem to talk to you.
They do not object. They have more important things to do now.
You go quietly. One of the knights turns his head, very slowly, to watch you go.

events.title: The Pedlar of Wrong Notes
events.text: A man with a cart full of junk and a bell that rings slightly off. Bits of tin hang from his hat and chime against each other on purpose. 'The song is out of tune,' he says, 'so everything is for sale.' The wares are different every time you look.

outcome.text: You open it. It is fog. Good fog, though.
Mostly. The bits that are wrong are wrong in an interesting way.
The heads stop hearing each other for an afternoon, and all of them feel much better.
Signed by a bishop who does not exist, sealed by one who does. The Order accepts it with a sigh.

choices.text: Buy something warm in a box.

outcome.text: Don't open the box. You can feel it through the box. Things that eat heat will smell it on you.
He leans in. 'A hoard,' he whispers, 'a real one, and nobody guarding it but a hole.' He points. You are fairly sure he points.
He pays in muck, and wears the skin as a hat at once.
His bell rings off-key behind you for a long time.

events.title: The Rumoured Hoard
events.text: Where the pedlar pointed: a hole. At the bottom of the hole, something glints. Next to the hole, a sign in the pedlar's handwriting: HOARD. NOT A TRAP.

success.text: It was not a trap. It was, against every expectation, a hoard.

failure.text: It was not a trap, strictly. It was a hole, and you were in it for some time.

outcome.text: The Strangler's long neck reaches the glint without the rest of you. A small hoard, honestly come by.
Very wise. Somewhere the pedlar is a little hurt.

events.title: The Dead Letter Box
events.text: A box nailed to a post where three tunnels meet: POST FOR THE BRETHREN BELOW. COLLECTED WEEKLY. Nobody has collected it in years. It is stuffed with letters.

outcome.text: 'Brother, the patrols are moved to the east galleries. Do not tell the hydra.' Nobody told the hydra. The hydra read it.

choices.text: Read the one with the map.

outcome.text: A brother's directions to a cellar where he hid his wine. He has, the letter says, 'probably drunk it'.
It is very long and very sincere, and is about a candle. The heads are moved, against their will.
Forty pages on the state of the underground latrines. You learn where the latrines are, and that is information.
Paper and sealing wax. The brethren below will never know what they missed.

events.title: A Brother's Cellar
events.text: A small cellar behind a loose stone. Inside: nine bottles, eight empty, one full, and a brother of the Order asleep among them, smiling.

success.text: Strong, sweet, and holy. The heads sing. None of them in the same song.

failure.text: Strong, sweet and holy, and the heads sing very loudly, and the brother wakes up and joins in, and then runs.

choices.text: Take the bottle, leave the brother.

outcome.text: Muck for the bottle, and the brother sleeps on. When he wakes, he will blame himself.
Very relaxed.

events.title: The One Coil Sends Regards
events.text: Across the tunnel someone has stretched a rope with a single knot in it, and from the rope hangs a snake skin with every head but one cut off. A note: THE SERPENT IS ONE. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED. THIS IS THE SECOND WARNING.

success.text: Nothing happens. Then, far off, someone curses in a voice that has only one opinion.

failure.text: The rope was tied to the ceiling. The ceiling was tied to nothing.

outcome.text: You tie on knots for the missing heads, nine in all. The heads are proud of this. The One Coil will not be.
You take another tunnel. It is the long way, which is also a kind of warning.

events.title: A Still Pool
events.text: A still, black pool. Nothing happens here, which in the underground counts as an event.

outcome.text: Cold, clean, and quiet.
The heads doze off one by one. None at the same time, but it's a start.
